description: Required migration coverage inventory, not executable tests or proof of parity. Contract IDs identify groups; cases lists contain implemented test IDs only. Empty cases and pending status remain required work, even when other groups pass. Operation tuples are a pinned scope snapshot, not a second authoritative catalogue.

contracts.description: Run help, version, docs and bundled model/rigging discovery through the actual executable with empty and invalid host configuration. Assert exit/stdout/stderr and no credentials, keyring, browser, network or persistent host side effects. Include root and every help/docs topic, aliases and parent-command defaults.

Reject unknown commands/options, repeated non-repeatable options, missing/extra arguments, command-inapplicable options, malformed selectors and conflicting input/stdin/authority flags before host effects. Preserve invalid_usage exit 2 versus interaction_required exit 1 and JSON error selection. Positive controls must prove the corresponding admitted command reaches its owner.

Preserve public result/error envelopes, stdout/stderr roles, exits 0/1/2, null/zero/negative credit facts, integer-cent formatting, safe organization choices, task receipts and partial-save reports. Escape terminal controls in human output while retaining JSON values; never print raw errors, stack traces, credential bytes, provider bodies or warnings. Closed output pipes must fail safely.

Cover grida with no args, -h/--help, help [topic], topic --help and bare command-group defaults across every Cli.topics entry. Unknown topics and incompatible flags fail; provider help includes shared-store/manual-edit guidance without opening custody. Human layout changes need an explicit compatibility decision.
Cover -v and --version with the packaged version and newline; no host initialization. Positional commands and unrelated flags reject instead of selecting another operation.
Cover docs and docs [topic] for every known help topic, canonical guide ownership and no fetch/browser launch. Reject unknown topics/options; validate installed links against built documentation.

Cover default keyring choice, explicit file/keyring choice, saved backend retention, system browser and --no-browser manual URL on stderr. Refuse --json/--no-input; return only safe identity/expiry after verified commit. Cover denied/failed/cancelled ceremonies without replacing a valid prior session.

Read safe local session state without online verification. Signed-out is a successful status DTO with exit 1; signed-in/refresh-needed exit 0. Never expose credentials or turn malformed/unavailable established custody into signed-out.

Clear local credentials durably and request only session-local remote revocation. confirmed/not-needed exit 0; unconfirmed exits 1 with local sign-out retained. Cover already signed-out, offline/expired revocation, custody failure and newer-login races without restoring old credentials.
Return backend/profile/initialization/migration metadata without reading credential secrets, starting login or checking keyring access. Preserve malformed-store and host configuration failures.

Accept only explicit keyring/file destination, preserve revision/profile identity, settle started mutations on signals, and report safe storage state. Cover same backend, both directions, copy/read-back/retirement failures and resumable migration; no implicit fallback.

Verify identity first, then gather complete projected memberships through terminal cursor, including empty accounts and short nonterminal pages. Permit completion on page 100; refuse exhaustion, stalled cursors, later-page failure or signed-out rather than returning partial success. Never launch login.

Cover explicit slug/id and sole-membership selection; numeric slug remains a slug. Preserve cached unknown/zero/negative USD cents, timestamp and server billing gate. Ambiguity exposes bounded safe choices; missing membership, refusal and invalid selectors cause no fallback, login or inferred credit eligibility.

Report supported BYOK key presence, effective source, expected environment name and shared plaintext storage without secrets, provider verification or account login. Preserve malformed explicit key and corrupt/pending store errors instead of reporting absence; GG remains a separate unchecked login authority.

Cover each supported provider through hidden prompt or --key-stdin, never keys on argv. Validate first; check OpenRouter/Vercel/fal/Tripo once before opening or changing custody; ElevenLabs returns not_supported without a request. Denied/unavailable/invalid/cancelled checks preserve old keys. Settle a durable write already started; JSON/no-input require stdin.

Remove only the selected shared stored key, including durable pre-import tombstones. Do not read ambient keys, revoke at the provider or sign out Grida. Fresh readers observe removal while an explicit environment key can remain effective; pending/corrupt/unsafe stores fail unchanged.

Cover provider/kind/modality/local-image filters, staged and deprecated executable routes and schema-derived local_image_flags. Ordinary list is offline. --available requires explicit provider: BYOK checks selected key presence without probe; GG reads selected organization's cached gate online without minting a grant or promising readiness.

Require explicit provider/model, infer kind only if unambiguous, preserve default and explicitly selected variants, and return the full schema in JSON with corresponding human input guidance. Unknown/unavailable routes fail without authority or provider fallback; retained historical bindings remain inspectable.

Cover all exact tuples in operation_inventory for image/video/music/sound-effect/text-to-speech/three-d. Validate selected operation, friendly or JSON input and fresh output destination before authority/submission. Preserve explicit provider/model/variant and scoped GG versus BYOK. Save returned bytes plus receipt; failures/cancellation retain safe paid-work identity and partial files without replay.

Allow only explicit ElevenLabs with selected env/stdin/store key and no Grida login. Project/deduplicate/sort public voices; preserve paging caps and terminal/partial semantics. Later-page denial, malformed pages, cycles, timeout or cancellation must not become successful partial data outside the documented cap behavior.

List Tripo and GG rig-check/rigging descriptors with optional provider/feature filters, entirely offline. Eligibility has structured output and no model identity; paid rigging has a specific model and GLB output.

Require tripo/gg and rig-check/rigging; refuse model for rig-check and require model for rigging. Return selected input/output schemas without custody/network, distinguishing invalid selector from absent model.

Accept exactly explicit local mesh or JSON input with one stdin owner; check on selected Tripo BYOK or GG authority. Return riggable, rig_type and safe task metadata; riggable=false still exits 0. Never submit rigging or write generated artifacts. Reject malformed/oversized/unsupported mesh before authority; preserve accepted-task failures.

Require explicit supported rig model, fresh output directory and exact mesh+rig-type+spec or JSON input. Run independently of any earlier check; preserve model-specific rig types/specifications, Tripo/GG separation, GLB bytes and task receipt. Never overwrite/replay; save returned paid bytes even when interrupted and report partial publication safely.

Use only bundled hosted client/issuer/API/callback registration, or the explicit trusted local fixture configuration. Reject arbitrary origin/client overrides, invalid/local-as-hosted fixtures and absent/unsafe files without hosted fallback. Cwd/dotenv discovery never grants authority; public admission-key rotation must not change profile identity.

Preserve default and absolute GRIDA_HOME handling, canonicalize permitted OS home aliases at the host boundary, isolate local fixture custody and fail empty/relative/ordinary-home aliases appropriately. Provider store receives one canonical home; its stricter path checks must not be bypassed. Cover missing descendants and platform-limited stored credentials while preserving explicit Windows env/stdin.

Launch only the validated trusted authorization URL with argument-safe platform browser invocation or explicit manual output. Cover malformed destinations, launcher errors/timeouts, cancellation and unsupported platforms; never expose raw host errors or silently substitute manual/browser mode.

Test real executable SIGINT/SIGTERM during startup, login, credential acquisition/mutation, network work and artifact publication. Refuse new work after interruption; clean listeners and login resources; let started native writes and already-returned paid bytes settle. No forced exit, automatic logout, credential rollback or replay.

Validate exact ID/slug selectors before I/O; choose automatically only one terminal membership. Explicit lookup follows at most 100 progressing pages, no first-member fallback or selection cache. Preserve no_organizations/organization_required/organization_not_found/selection_unavailable distinctions, bounded choices and fresh server authorization after selection.

Preserve only fixed organizations.list and credits.read paths and canonical input fields, response projection, ordered safe-integer IDs and cursor semantics. Credits preserve all allowed cache/billing states and reject inconsistent/mismatched schemas. No generic authenticated fetch, automatic read replay, implicit login or inference of model readiness.

Known vectors must preserve profile hash serialization/key order, canonical home, issuer/client/API binding, on-disk names and native item lookup identity. Public admission-key rotation leaves profile/revision unchanged. Reject rebound or malformed envelopes and never adopt untracked keyring credentials after metadata loss.

Prove PKCE/live-identity login commit, local status, 30-second refresh window, one-use refresh rotation saved before follow-up acceptance, generation/revision fences and session-local logout. Test stale verify/login/refresh results, cancelled writes, old logout versus new login and identity/network failure after accepted rotation without resurrecting or rolling back spent credentials.

Exercise real registered loopback ports, bind before browser, fallback only among registered ports, exact path/method/host/state/issuer and duplicate-parameter admission, denial, two-minute expiry, socket cleanup and cancellation. Bound token requests/bodies, refuse redirects and raw upstream error output.

Preserve versioned metadata/envelope/revision/tombstone/backend semantics, established missing-item failures, explicit backend choice and no silent keyring-to-file fallback. Require native write completion and read-back; retain committed mutations after later failures and reject malformed/rebound/oversized data without recovery overwrite.

Test both file/keyring migration directions and every copy/publication/retirement failure boundary. Resume the recorded destination without adopting stale source or reviving old authority; remove plaintext or clear old native secret only in the accepted order. Include cancellation and uncertain post-publication failure.

Run TS/TS, TS/Rust, Rust/TS and Rust/Rust real-process pairings against disposable shared custody. Prove one-use refresh rotation, verify versus refresh, logout versus in-flight login/newer login, process restart and migration crash recovery. Historical supported artifacts must be selected explicitly; current source-only success is insufficient.

Use disposable synthetic native entries on macOS and Linux to prove TS keytar/Rust item read-write-tombstone compatibility, service/account/Secret Service attributes, access behavior, absence versus failure and write/read-back integrity. Cover locked/unavailable/permission-denied stores without file fallback; mocked bindings alone do not satisfy this gate.

Rust-specific proof: cancelling or dropping an async waiter must not release SQLite/profile authority while a started blocking native credential mutation or its read-back continues. Use competing processes and controlled mutation completion; verify subsequent custody remains ordered, including failed write/read-back.

Reuse raw protocol fixtures and add boundary vectors for TOML 1.1, strict UTF-8/no BOM, exact key bytes, integer version, exact schema, nesting/byte/provider bounds, unknown versions, escaping and tombstones. Missing file is empty unstarted; corrupt/unsupported/unsafe/pending is not absence. Invalid cases leave canonical bytes untouched and expose fixed safe failure codes.

Use real files to verify owner/mode/ACL/no-follow/hardlink/inode rules and safe existing ancestors without chmod repair. Writes use exclusive private temp, fsync, atomic rename and parent fsync; failures after rename never restore older data. Validate and discard only matching orphan temps; never adopt them. Test symlink/special-file/ACL races and injected publication/fsync failures; SIGKILL is not power-loss proof.

Preserve stable zero-byte SQLite inode, BEGIN IMMEDIATE/ROLLBACK exclusion, no schema/commit/WAL or unlink, safe journal/sidecar checks, process-local descriptor serialization, busy-only retries and bounded acquisition. Held work outlives acquisition deadline; cancellation never steals/releases a live holder. Test independent processes/module copies and crash release.

Prove source-writer-before-canonical lock order, canonical value/tombstone precedence, durable unstarted-to-pending publication before source retirement and pending-to-complete only after durable idempotent retirement. Resume retirement without reimport after crash; preserve unrelated source OAuth records. Failed/uncertain publication cannot retire source; pending blocks ordinary operations.

Run all TS/Rust reader-writer pairings on real shared provider files and SQLite locks. Cover exact values, concurrent disjoint/same-provider updates, deletion/restart tombstones, migration fences and crashed writers. Include supported Desktop-owned source retirement; older writers that ignore the protocol cannot be silently declared compatible.

Only selected provider authority is inspected. Explicit stdin wins over exact supported environment variable then shared store; blank/malformed explicit values fail rather than fall back. Environment/stdin bypass custody and never persist. No aliases/inherited values/dotenv, GG-as-BYOK or cross-provider fallback. Bound raw stdin bytes, timeout/cancellation and hidden prompt restoration without echo.

Preserve shared static normalization and provider-specific accepted key forms, raw-byte bounds and fixed verification endpoints. Explicit checks run once, admit read-only success without promising credits/model access, reject management credentials where required and project only safe statuses. ElevenLabs check is unsupported. Bound body/deadline/cancellation, reject redirects and never retain server/native diagnostics.

For every advertised operation, compare friendly CLI and JSON input after semantic normalization. Preserve absent/null/false/zero, safe integers, model-specific seed/options and Unicode length rules; reject unknown/unsupported fields and conflicts before reads or authority. Own input snapshots; validate URL/base64/GLB semantics beyond schema. Include exact byte limits, malformed raw UTF-8/JSON, BOM behavior and no path expansion from JSON.

Explicit cwd-relative grants only; bounded one-time JSON/text/image/mesh reads, content-based PNG/JPEG/static-WebP/GLB admission, growth/cancellation races and aggregate base64 budget. Reserve new output under existing parent before authority, probe atomic publication, exclusively save bytes/hashes/receipt and never overwrite. Partial save retains published paths/task metadata; abandon removes only an empty owned reservation.

Input/operation/output refusal must precede key/account access and submission. Selected BYOK never consults Grida login or another provider; selected GG never inspects BYOK. Separate account, scoped GG, provider requests, signed upload and public-download authority; no credential-bearing arbitrary URLs or implicit provider/model/billing fallback.

Prove fixed route/method/header/body admission, DNS address validation and pinning with original TLS authority, no ambient proxies/cookies, no authenticated redirects/replay and reviewed credential-free download redirects. Check each redirected DNS result, mixed public/private answers, response/body bounds, multipart/signed-upload limits, whole deadlines, cancellation/late work and safe errors. Resolve reqwest fit using behavior, not Node internals.

Every pending operation tuple needs admitted request/result plus meaningful invalid/failure/cancellation cases through the real adapter. Preserve one accepted paid submission, explicit batching ceiling, no retry after ambiguous submission, safe accepted-task identity, polling/SSE completion versus premature EOF, credential lifetime and cumulative time/byte limits. No paid provider calls in deterministic conformance.

Verify selected membership followed by one scoped memory-only GG mint, safe metadata versus actual grant distinction, fixed hosted/local-fixture routes and live expiry checks. Never forward account tokens into media, persist/reuse grants across invocations, remint/retry or fall back to BYOK. Funded Tripo uses signed credential-free uploads and rechecks scoped authority before paid submission.

Cover exact image provider/model/text-reference bindings, provider controls and native-background eligibility; Vercel image wire, OpenRouter unified images, fal queues and GG fixed route. Preserve bounded image counts, provider batch splitting, ordering/result-byte limits, MIME admission and secret-safe failure. SDK-native automatic resolution is not a new CLI feature.

Cover exact text/image bindings and model-specific options, including inline versus URL-only frame admission and fal Veo Lite audio control. Exercise Vercel SSE result/error/EOF, OpenRouter authenticated polling/content, fal queue and GG envelopes with one submission, bounded frame/body/result budgets and cancellation. Preserve the zero-seed restriction until an explicit approved divergence changes it.

Cover GG music and ElevenLabs sound-effect/speech exact wires. Preserve music trimmed UTF-16 lengths/safe seed, sound-effect trimmed code-point lengths and absent/false/zero options, and speech voice normalization with unchanged Unicode text. Project only admitted audio bytes, fixed formats and bounded deadlines/bodies; errors or access loss do not replay.

Cover fal exact text/image routes and Tripo h3.1/p1/p2 text/image/multiview across BYOK and GG. Preserve per-model input/options, bounded PNG/JPEG upload, exact task/model/type identity and polling, reviewed GLB download and self-contained GLB validation. Retain safe task IDs/credit refusals; no substitution or repeated paid submission after loss/timeout.

Cover standalone model-free eligibility and rig-v1.0/rig-v2.5-specific rigging on Tripo/GG, mesh validation, exact rig types/specifications and accepted observed legacy task kinds. Preserve structured negative success versus paid GLB results, task identity and credits. Bound uploads/polling/downloads and retain accepted tasks on cancellation, transport or publication failure without resubmission.

Pin exact discovery/inspection tuples, schemas, listed/staged/deprecated status, binding identities and local-image metadata. Preserve existing TS/web schema-1 snapshot projections, pinned snapshot rejection/removal semantics and bundled families outside refresh projection. CLI discovery stays bundled/offline; catalogue refresh APIs outside CLI are not automatically Rust port scope.

Make authored JSON/schema the shared source with deterministic TS/Rust generated consumers, bundled references and explicit semantic normalization. Check generated drift, unchanged TS/web behavior and package completeness; ordinary Rust build must not need Node, network or paths outside its Cargo package. Prototype representative schemas before selecting type generation.

Test the actual packed npm candidate set and native target selection, executable bits, version coupling, spaces in paths, streams/signals and absence of optional binaries. Preserve grida command and supported Windows env/stdin behavior. Exercise local installed OAuth, synthetic provider/media/rigging and supported historical TS/Desktop compatibility before replacement; source tests alone do not prove installability.

Check canonical guide examples, exhaustive command/help/docs ownership and built routes using the actual installed candidate. Update Node-only guidance when packaging changes and maintain third-party notices for shipped Rust dependencies and launcher contents.

Implement and test build-once/package-once exact-hash publication, matched versions, provenance and platform-first/root-last ordering. Preserve manual/main-only/environment gates; reject missing target proof, partial-release mismatch and unsupported libc. The real eight-platform execution and deployed-account/provider checks are mandatory release_acceptance prerequisites, outside a local pre-PR run.

operation_inventory.captured_from: MediaOperations.list() and MediaOperations.rigging.list(), importing current TypeScript source after fresh baseline workspace builds. Each tuple needs positive request/result and meaningful negative/failure/cancellation cases before completion.

divergences.description: Current shared/native input validation rejects zero seed for Vercel video because the pinned JS adapter cannot represent it. Rust may remove the SDK limitation, but zero remains a required rejection until the compatibility decision and shared expectations explicitly change.
divergences.decision: Preserve the pinned TypeScript adapter’s Vercel video seed-zero rejection. Rust-native internals do not authorize changing the public contract.

divergences.description: Command grammar, guidance and canonical URLs must remain; byte-for-byte human help layout is not yet ratified. Clap defaults must not silently change accepted aliases, incompatible-option refusal, exit codes or stdout/stderr behavior. Update installed docs checks explicitly if layout changes.
divergences.decision: Preserve current help prose byte-for-byte in owned Rust assets for the first slice. All 27 topics compared with the pinned reference on 2026-10-01; no intentional layout divergence introduced.

release_acceptance.note: These execution prerequisites belong to release/CI after the pre-PR implementation handoff. Local conformance does not claim that remote CI or hosted acceptance has run.
requirements: All eight real platform binaries build and the same exact npm archives pass the target-native installed matrix; fixture headers are rejected by publication.
The exact candidate passes installed documentation and local OAuth/account/media proofs in release CI.
Hosted registration/consent/account/GG and appropriate live-provider acceptance remain required by the existing release procedure; deterministic tests never spend provider credits.
